{خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ}
 
{وَنَهَى النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ يَطُوفَ بِالْبَيْتِ عُرْيَانَا}
 فَالصَّلَاةُ أَوْلَى. وَسُئِلَ عَنْ الصَّلَاةِ فِي الثَّوْبِ الْوَاحِدِ.
 فَقَالَ:
 " 
{أو لِكُلِّكُمْ ثَوْبَانِ؟}
translated_text:
of silver worn on the toes. This was reported by Ibn Abī Hātim. This shows that women initially used to expose their feet, just as they exposed their faces and hands. They would let their hems hang down, yet a woman’s foot might become visible as she walked; they did not wear leather socks or shoes. Covering the feet during prayer entails great hardship.

Umm Salamah said:

“A woman should pray in a garment long enough to cover the tops of her feet.”

Yet when she prostrates, the soles of her feet may become visible.

In short, scriptural evidence and scholarly consensus establish that, when praying at home, she need not wear the outer garment that covers her; that is required only when she goes out. Thus, she may pray at home even with her face, hands and feet visible, just as women initially used to walk about before they were commanded to draw their outer garments over themselves. The limits of the awrah—the parts of the body requiring concealment—in prayer therefore do not correspond, in either direction, to those applicable to being seen by others.

When Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the apparent adornment meant clothing, he did not say that her entire body, down to her nails, is awrah. Rather, that is Ahmad’s statement, meaning that such covering is a condition of prayer.

The jurists call this “Chapter on Covering the Awrah.” Yet this is not an expression used by the Messenger, nor do the Quran and Sunnah state that whatever a worshipper covers is awrah. Rather, Allah Most High said:

“Take your adornment at every place of prayer.”

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) forbade circumambulating the House naked, so this applies all the more to prayer. He was asked about praying in a single garment and replied:

“Does every one of you have two garments?”

translated_text:
And he said concerning a single garment:

“If it is ample, wrap it around yourself; if it is narrow, wrap it around your waist.”

“He forbade a man to pray in a single garment with none of it covering his shoulder.”

This shows that a man is commanded during prayer to cover his awrah—the thighs and other parts—even if we allow another man to look at them. If, according to one of the two views—which is also one of the two positions reported from Ahmad—we say that the awrah consists of the front and rear private parts and that the thigh is not awrah, this concerns whether another man may look at it; it does not concern prayer or circumambulation. A man may not pray with his thighs uncovered, whether or not they are considered awrah, nor may he circumambulate naked. Rather, he must pray wearing a garment; this is indispensable. If it is narrow, he wraps it around his waist, and if it is ample, he wraps it around himself. Likewise, even if he prays alone in a house, he must cover those parts, by scholarly consensus.

As for a man praying with his thighs exposed when he is able to wear a waist-wrapper, this is impermissible, and there should be no disagreement about it. Those who have based this question on the two positions reported concerning the awrah, as some have done, are mistaken. Neither Ahmad nor anyone else said that a worshipper may pray in this state. How could that be, when Ahmad commands him to cover his shoulders? How, then, could he permit him to uncover his thigh? That, then, is the point.

translated_text:
Scholars have differed over whether a man must cover his awrah when alone, but they have not differed over the necessity of clothing during prayer. By scholarly consensus, a person may not pray naked when able to clothe himself. For this reason, Ahmad and others permitted those without clothing to pray seated, with their imam in their midst, unlike the situation outside prayer. This prohibition is not based on whether others can see them.

In the hadith narrated by Bahz ibn Hakīm, from his father, from his grandfather, the latter said:

“I asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, what if one of us is alone?’ He replied, ‘Allah is more deserving of your modesty than people are.’”

If this applies outside prayer, then Allah is all the more deserving of one's modesty during prayer. One should therefore dress becomingly for intimate discourse with Him, glorified is He.

For this reason, when Ibn Umar saw his servant Nāfiʿ praying bareheaded, he asked him, “Tell me, if you were going out among people, would you go out like this?” He replied, “No.” Ibn Umar said, “Allah is more deserving that you dress becomingly for Him.”

Likewise, in an authentic hadith, when the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—was told, “A man likes his clothes and shoes to look good,” he replied:

“Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.”

This is akin to the command that the worshipper observe ritual purity and cleanliness and use perfume. The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—commanded that places of prayer be established in homes and kept clean and perfumed. Accordingly, a person should cover more fully during prayer than a man must before another man or a woman before another woman. For this reason, a woman is commanded to cover her head during prayer. As for her face

and her hands and feet, she was forbidden to expose them only to unrelated men, not to women or her male relatives whom she is permanently forbidden to marry. It is thus clear that these do not fall into the same category as the awrah that a man must conceal from another man or a woman from another woman, whose exposure is forbidden because of its indecency and ugliness.

Rather, exposing these parts is a precursor to sexual immorality, so prohibiting their exposure was a prohibition of what leads to sexual immorality, as He says in the verse:

“That is purer for you.”

And in the verse concerning the screen, He says:

“That is purer for your hearts and their hearts.”

This was therefore prohibited to block the means to wrongdoing, not because these parts are unconditionally awrah, whether in prayer or otherwise. That, then, is the distinction.

Requiring a woman to cover her hands during prayer is very far-fetched. The hands prostrate just as the face does. Women in the time of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—had only tunics, and they carried out their tasks wearing them. A woman would expose her hands when kneading, grinding grain and baking. Had covering the hands during prayer been obligatory, the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—would have made that clear. The same applies to the feet.

He prescribed only a head-covering in addition to the tunic, so they prayed in their tunics and head-coverings:

“As for the garment that a woman would let trail, she asked the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—about it, and he said, ‘A handspan.’ They said, ‘Then their lower legs will be exposed.’ He said, ‘A cubit, and they must not exceed that.’”

And the words of Umar ibn Abī Rabīah:

translated_text:
“Slaughter and battle are decreed for us;
For fair women, the trailing of hems.”

This applied when women went out of their homes. Hence the report:

“He was asked about a woman who trails her hem over a filthy place, and replied, ‘What it passes over afterward purifies it.’”

Inside her home, however, a woman did not wear such clothing. Likewise, women later adopted leather footwear to cover their lower legs when going out, but did not wear it inside their homes. This is why they said, “Then their lower legs will be exposed.” The purpose was therefore to cover the lower leg, because when a garment ends above the ankles, the lower leg becomes exposed while walking.

It has also been reported:

“Deprive women of clothing, and they will remain in their secluded chambers.”

This means that if a woman had no clothing to wear when going out, she would remain at home. Muslim women used to pray in their homes. The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from attending the mosques of Allah, though their homes are better for them.”

In addition to their tunics, they were instructed to wear only head-coverings. A woman was not instructed to wear trousers, because her tunic sufficed. Nor was she instructed to cover her feet with leather footwear or socks, or to cover her hands with gloves or anything else. This indicates that she is not obliged to cover these parts during prayer when no unrelated men are present.

It has also been reported:

“The angels do not look upon concealed adornment. When a woman removes her head-covering and tunic, they do not look at her.”

A hadith concerning this has also been related from Khadījah.

original_text:
فَهَذَا الْقَدْرُ لِلْقَمِيصِ وَالْخِمَارِ هُوَ الْمَأْمُورُ بِهِ لِحَقِّ الصَّلَاةِ كَمَا يُؤْمَرُ الرَّجُلُ إذَا صَلَّى فِي ثَوْبٍ وَاسِعٍ أَنْ يَلْتَحِفَ بِهِ فَيُغَطِّي عَوْرَتَهُ وَمَنْكِبَيْهِ فَالْمَنْكِبَانِ فِي حَقِّهِ كَالرَّأْسِ فِي حَقِّ الْمَرْأَةِ لِأَنَّهُ يُصَلِّي فِي قَمِيصٍ أَوْ مَا يَقُومُ مَقَامَ الْقَمِيصِ. وَهُوَ فِي الْإِحْرَامِ لَا يَلْبَسُ عَلَى بَدَنِهِ مَا يُقَدِّرُ لَهُ كَالْقَمِيصِ وَالْجُبَّةِ كَمَا أَنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ لَا تَنْتَقِبُ وَلَا تَلْبَسُ الْقُفَّازَيْنِ. وَأَمَّا رَأْسُهُ فَلَا يُخَمِّرُهُ وَوَجْهُ الْمَرْأَةِ فِيهِ قَوْلَانِ فِي مَذْهَبِ أَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِ؛
 قِيلَ:
 إنَّهُ كَرَأْسِ الرَّجُلِ فَلَا يُغَطَّى.
 وَقِيلَ:
 إنَّهُ كَيَدَيْهِ فَلَا تُغَطَّى بِالنِّقَابِ وَالْبُرْقُعِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا صُنِعَ عَلَى قَدْرِهِ وَهَذَا هُوَ الصَّحِيحُ؛ فَإِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمْ يَنْهَ إلَّا عَنْ الْقُفَّازَيْنِ وَالنِّقَابِ. وَكُنَّ النِّسَاءُ يُدْنِينَ عَلَى وُجُوهِهِنَّ مَا يَسْتُرُهَا مِنْ الرِّجَالِ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَضْعِ مَا يُجَافِيهَا عَنْ الْوَجْهِ فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ وَجْهَهَا كَيَدَيْ الرَّجُلِ وَيَدَيْهَا؛ وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الْمَرْأَةَ كُلَّهَا عَوْرَةٌ كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ فَلَهَا أَنْ تُغَطِّيَ وَجْهَهَا وَيَدَيْهَا لَكِنْ بِغَيْرِ اللِّبَاسِ الْمَصْنُوعِ بِقَدْرِ الْعُضْوِ كَمَا أَنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَا يَلْبَسُ السَّرَاوِيلَ وَيَلْبَسُ الْإِزَارَ وَاَللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
Thus, this extent of covering with the tunic and head-covering is what is prescribed for prayer itself, just as a man praying in a roomy garment is instructed to wrap it around himself, covering the parts of his body that must be concealed as well as his shoulders. His shoulders are therefore comparable to a woman’s head in this respect, since he prays in a tunic or something serving the same purpose.

While in ihrām, he must not wear garments tailored to fit his body, such as a tunic or robe, just as a woman must not wear a niqāb (face-veil) or gloves. He must not cover his head. As for a woman’s face, there are two views in the school of Ahmad and those of other scholars:

One view holds that it is like a man’s head and therefore must not be covered.

The other holds that it is like his hands: it must not be covered with a niqāb, a burqu' (face-covering), or anything similar made to fit it. This is the correct view, for the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—prohibited only gloves and the niqāb. Women used to lower coverings over their faces to conceal them from men, without placing anything beneath them to keep them away from the face. This shows that a woman’s face is like a man’s hands and her own hands.

This is because a woman’s entire body is to be covered, as explained above. She may therefore cover her face and hands, but not with garments made to fit the particular part of the body, just as a man must not wear trousers but may wear a waist-wrapper. And Allah, glorified and exalted be He, knows best.

وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ الصَّلَاةِ فِي النَّعْلِ وَنَحْوِهِ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
أَمَّا الصَّلَاةُ فِي النَّعْلِ وَنَحْوِهِ مِثْلَ الْجُمْجُمِ وَالْمَدَاسِ والزربول وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ:
 فَلَا يُكْرَهُ بَلْ هُوَ مُسْتَحَبٌّ؛ لِمَا ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ 
{عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُصَلِّي فِي نَعْلَيْهِ}
 .
 وَفِي السُّنَنِ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{إنَّ الْيَهُودَ لَا يُصَلُّونَ فِي نِعَالِهِمْ فَخَالِفُوهُمْ}
 فَأَمَرَ بِالصَّلَاةِ فِي النِّعَالِ مُخَالَفَةً لِلْيَهُودِ. وَإِذَا عُلِمَتْ طَهَارَتُهَا لَمْ تُكْرَهْ الصَّلَاةُ فِيهَا بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَمَّا إذَا تُيُقِّنَ نَجَاسَتُهَا فَلَا يُصَلِّي فِيهَا حَتَّى تُطَهَّرَ. لَكِنَّ الصَّحِيحَ أَنَّهُ إذَا دُلِكَ النَّعْلُ بِالْأَرْضِ طَهُرَ بِذَلِكَ. كَمَا جَاءَتْ بِهِ السُّنَّةُ سَوَاءٌ كَانَتْ النَّجَاسَةُ عُذْرَةً أَوْ غَيْرَ عُذْرَةٍ. فَإِنَّ أَسْفَلَ النَّعْلِ مَحَلُّ تَكَرُّرِ مُلَاقَاةِ النَّجَاسَةِ لَهُ فَهُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ السَّبِيلَيْنِ فَلَمَّا كَانَ إزَالَتُهُ عَنْهَا بِالْحِجَارَةِ ثَابِتًا بِالسُّنَّةِ الْمُتَوَاتِرَةِ فَكَذَلِكَ هَذَا.
translated_text:
He was asked about praying in sandals and similar footwear.

He replied:

Praying in sandals and similar footwear, such as the jumjum, madās, zarbūl and other kinds, is not disliked; rather, it is recommended. It is established in the Sahīh that “the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—used to pray in his sandals.” In the Sunan, he is reported to have said:

“The Jews do not pray in their sandals, so differ from them.”

Thus, he commanded praying in sandals to differ from the Jews. If they are known to be free of ritual impurity, praying in them is not disliked, by agreement of the Muslims. If, however, they are definitely known to be impure, one must not pray in them until they have been purified.

The correct view, however, is that rubbing sandals against the ground purifies them, as stated in the Sunnah, whether the impurity is feces or something else. The soles of sandals repeatedly come into contact with impurity, so they are comparable to the urinary and anal openings. Since removing impurity from those openings with stones is established by the Sunnah through mass transmission, the same applies here.

original_text:
وَإِذَا شَكَّ فِي نَجَاسَةٍ أَسْفَلَ الْخُفِّ لَمْ تُكْرَهْ الصَّلَاةُ فِيهِ وَلَوْ تَيَقَّنَ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ أَنَّهُ كَانَ نَجِسًا فَلَا إعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ فِي الصَّحِيحِ كَذَلِكَ غَيْرُهُ كَالْبَدَنِ وَالثِّيَابِ وَالْأَرْضِ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ لُبْسِ الْقَبَاءِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ إذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يُدْخِلَ يَدَيْهِ فِي أَكْمَامِهِ هَلْ يُكْرَهُ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ. فَإِنَّ الْفُقَهَاءَ ذَكَرُوا جَوَازَ ذَلِكَ؛ وَلَيْسَ هُوَ مِثْلَ السَّدْلِ الْمَكْرُوهِ لِمَا فِيهِ مِنْ مُشَابَهَةِ الْيَهُودِ؛ فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ اللُّبْسَةَ لَيْسَتْ مِنْ مَلَابِسِ الْيَهُودِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ الْفِرَاءِ مِنْ جُلُودِ الْوُحُوشِ هَلْ تَجُوزُ الصَّلَاةُ فِيهَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، أَمَّا جِلْدُ الْأَرْنَبِ فَتَجُوزُ الصَّلَاةُ فِيهِ بِلَا رَيْبٍ وَأَمَّا الثَّعْلَبُ فَفِيهِ نِزَاعٌ وَالْأَظْهَرُ جَوَازُ الصَّلَاةِ فِيهِ وَجِلْدُ الضَّبُعِ كَذَلِكَ كُلُّ جِلْدٍ غَيْرِ جُلُودِ السِّبَاعِ التي نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ لُبْسِهَا.
translated_text:
If one is unsure whether there is impurity on the sole of a leather sock, praying in it is not disliked. Even if one discovers with certainty after the prayer that it was impure, one need not repeat the prayer, according to the correct view. The same applies to impurity on the body, clothing or ground.

He was asked:

Is wearing a coat during prayer disliked if one intends to put one’s arms into its sleeves?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. There is nothing wrong with that, for the jurists have stated that it is permissible. It is not like the disapproved manner of draping a garment, which involves resembling the Jews, since this way of wearing a coat is not characteristic of Jewish dress. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Is it permissible to pray in fur garments made from the skins of wild animals?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. As for rabbit skin, it is undoubtedly permissible to pray in it. As for fox skin, there is disagreement, but the stronger view is that praying in it is permissible. The same applies to hyena skin and to every skin other than the skins of predatory beasts, which the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—forbade wearing.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ الْمَرْأَةِ إذَا ظَهَرَ شَيْءٌ مِنْ شَعْرِهَا فِي الصَّلَاةِ هَلْ تَبْطُلُ صَلَاتُهَا أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا انْكَشَفَ شَيْءٌ يَسِيرٌ مِنْ شَعْرِهَا وَبَدَنِهَا لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَيْهَا الْإِعَادَةُ عِنْدَ أَكْثَرِ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَأَحْمَد، وَإِنْ انْكَشَفَ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ أَعَادَتْ الصَّلَاةَ فِي الْوَقْتِ عِنْدَ عَامَّةِ الْعُلَمَاءِ الْأَئِمَّةِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ الْمَرْأَةِ إذَا صَلَّتْ وَظَاهِرُ قَدَمِهَا مَكْشُوفٌ، هَلْ تَصِحُّ صَلَاتُهَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
هَذَا فِيهِ نِزَاعٌ بَيْنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَمَذْهَبُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ صَلَاتُهَا جَائِزَةٌ وَهُوَ أَحَدُ الْقَوْلَيْنِ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

If some of a woman’s hair becomes visible during prayer, does this invalidate her prayer?

He replied:

If a small amount of her hair or body becomes uncovered, she need not repeat the prayer according to most scholars. This is the position of Abū Hanīfa and Ahmad. If a substantial amount becomes uncovered, she must repeat the prayer within its prescribed time according to the generality of scholars, including the four imams and others. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

If a woman prays with the top of her foot uncovered, is her prayer valid?

He replied:

The scholars disagree on this. According to the school of Abū Hanīfa, her prayer is valid, and this is one of the two views.

original_text:
وَقَالَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
فَصْلٌ فِي 
" مَحَبَّةِ الْجَمَالِ "
 
(*)
ثَبَتَ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
" 
{لَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ أَحَدٌ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ إيمَانٍ وَلَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ أَحَدٌ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ حَبَّةِ خَرْدَلٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ مَنْ كَانَ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِثْقَالُ ذَرَّةٍ مِنْ كِبْرٍ فَقَالَ: رَجُلٌ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: إنَّ الرَّجُلَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ يَكُونَ ثَوْبُهُ حَسَنًا وَنَعْلُهُ حَسَنًا فَقَالَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ الْكِبْرُ بَطَرُ الْحَقِّ وَغَمْطُ النَّاسِ.}
 فَقَوْلُهُ: "
 
{إنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجِمَالَ}
 
" قَدْ أَدْرَجَ فِيهِ حُسْنَ الثِّيَابِ الَّتِي هِيَ الْمَسْئُولُ عَنْهَا فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْجَمِيلَ مِنْ النَّاسِ وَيَدْخُلُ فِي عُمُومِهِ بِطَرِيقِ الْفَحْوَى الْجَمِيلُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ.
 وَهَذَا كَقَوْلِهِ فِي الْحَدِيثِ الَّذِي رَوَاهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ:
 "
 
{إنَّ اللَّهَ نَظِيفٌ يُحِبُّ النَّظَافَةَ}
 
".
 وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ عَنْهُ فِي الصَّحِيحِ:
 "
 
{إنَّ اللَّهَ طَيِّبٌ لَا يَقْبَلُ إلَّا طَيِّبًا}
 "

هنا أمران:
الأول: أن هذا الفصل مستل من (الاستقامة) ١/ ٤٢٢ - ٤٣٥.
والثاني: أن الأخطاء - من سقط أو تصحيف - كثيرة في الموضعين: (الفتاوى) و (الاستقامة)، بعضها يصحح من بعض، وبعضها يصحح من السياق، لذلك اجتهدت في تصحيح هذا الفصل - والله المستعان - كما يلي:

translated_text:
He also said—may Allah have mercy on him:

Section on “Love of Beauty” (*)

It is established in Sahīh Muslim, on the authority of ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No one with an atom’s weight of faith in his heart will enter the Fire, and no one with a mustard seed’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.”

In another version: “No one with an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise.” A man said, “O Messenger of Allah, a man likes his clothes and shoes to be fine.” He replied, “Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.”

His words, “Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty,” include the fine clothing about which he was asked. Thus, it is understood that Allah loves what is beautiful in people, and, by implication, the statement’s general meaning encompasses what is beautiful in everything.

This is like his statement in the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhī:

“Allah is Clean and loves cleanliness.”

It is also authentically reported from him in the Sahīh:

“Allah is Pure and accepts only what is pure.”

وَهَذَا مِمَّا يُسْتَدَلُّ بِهِ عَلَى اسْتِحْبَابِ التَّجَمُّلِ فِي الْجُمَعِ وَالْأَعْيَادِ. كَمَا فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ

translated_text:
This is among the evidence used to establish that dressing well on Fridays and Eid festivals is recommended. As reported in the two Sahīh collections:

‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb saw a suit of clothes being sold in the market and said, “O Messenger of Allah, why not buy this to wear?” He replied, “Only someone who has no share in the Hereafter wears this.”

Supporting this concerning fine clothing is the report in the Sunan collections from Abū al-Ahwas al-Jushamī, who said:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw me wearing tattered clothes and asked, ‘Do you have any wealth?’ I replied, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘What kind of wealth?’ I replied, ‘All that Allah has given me, including camels and sheep.’ He said, ‘Then let Allah’s blessings and His generosity toward you be evident upon you.’”

These collections also report from ‘Amr ibn Shu‘ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah loves to see the effects of His blessings upon His servant.”

This, however, concerns displaying Allah’s blessings and the gratitude to Him that this entails, for He loves to be thanked; the earlier statement concerns love of beauty.

Some people have gone astray through their interpretation of this hadith, regarding it as contradictory. They reason that everything made by the Lord is beautiful, citing Allah’s words, Exalted is He:

“Who perfected everything He created,”

and therefore that He loves everything. They may also cite the saying of one of the shaykhs: “Love is a fire that burns away from the heart everything except what the beloved wills.”

and all created things are willed by Him. Some of these people explicitly ascribe beauty to everything without qualification. The least harm that befalls them is that they abandon zeal for Allah’s honour, forbidding wrong, hatred for Allah’s sake, striving in His path, and upholding His limits. Yet they contradict themselves in this, for they cannot be content with everything that exists. Wrongful things harm both them and others, so each is left to follow his own temperament and taste, and they cast off Allah’s religion.

Some may even embrace the doctrines of union with Allah and unrestricted divine indwelling. Others confine indwelling and union to particular created beings, such as the Messiah, ‘Alī, or others, or to shaykhs, kings, and beardless youths. They thus maintain that He dwells in beautiful forms and worship those forms.

Others do not hold this view, but instead regard love for beautiful forms—those of non-mahram women, beardless youths, and others—as an act of religious devotion. They consider this part of the beauty that Allah loves, and therefore love it themselves. They cloak forbidden natural attraction in religious love and turn what Allah has forbidden into a means of drawing nearer to Him:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency.’”

The other group says: It is established in Sahīh Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah does not look at your outward forms or your wealth; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds.”

Allah, Exalted is He, said of the hypocrites:

“When you see them, their bodies impress you.”

And He, Exalted is He, said:

“And how many generations We destroyed before them

who were finer in furnishings and appearance!” Furnishings means possessions, such as clothing and the like, while appearance means outward looks. He thus tells us that those He destroyed before them were more beautiful in appearance and had finer furnishings and greater wealth, showing that these things avail nothing with Him and carry no weight.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor any non-Arab to an Arab; no white person is superior to a black person, nor any black person to a white person, except through piety.”

It is also reported from him in the Sunan collections that he said:

“Plainness in dress is part of faith.”

Moreover, He has forbidden us certain things among the greatest beauties of this world: silk and gold attire, and vessels of gold and silver. Allah has forbidden boasting, arrogance, and clothing that expresses them, such as excessively long garments. Indeed, it is authentically reported that the Prophet said:

“Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.”

Similarly, an authentic report from Abū Hurayrah relates that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will not look at anyone who drags his lower garment out of conceit.”

Another authentic report, from Ibn ‘Umar, relates that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“While a man was dragging his lower garment out of arrogance, the earth swallowed him up, and he will continue sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection.”

Allah, Exalted is He, said:

“O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts and finery. But the clothing of righteousness—that is best. That is among the signs of Allah.”

He thus tells us that the clothing of righteousness is better than those things.

He, Exalted is He, also said:

“What of one brought up amid adornments, unable to make a clear case in dispute?”

And He, Exalted is He, said concerning Qārūn:

“So he came out before

his people in his finery.” They explained this as meaning crimson garments. Thus, it is authentically reported that ‘Abdullāh ibn ‘Amr said:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw me wearing two garments dyed with safflower and said, ‘These are garments of the disbelievers, so do not wear them.’ I asked, ‘Shall I wash them?’ He replied, ‘Burn them.’”

For this reason, the scholars disapproved of deeply saturated red, just as a prohibition has been reported concerning red saddle cushions. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb said, “Leave these bright garments to women.” Reports concerning this and similar matters are numerous.

Allah, Exalted is He, said:

“Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their chastity,”

through to His words:

“And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, so that you may succeed.”

In an authentic hadith, Jarīr ibn ‘Abdullāh reported:

“I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about an accidental glance. He said, ‘Avert your gaze.’”

In the Sunan collections, it is reported that he said to ‘Alī:

“O ‘Alī, do not follow one glance with another. The first is allowed you, but the second is not.”

Allah, Exalted is He, also said:

“And do not gaze longingly at what We have given some groups of them to enjoy—the splendour of worldly life—by which We test them. Your Lord’s provision is better and more lasting.”

And He said:

“Do not gaze longingly at what We have given some groups of them to enjoy, nor grieve over them, and lower your wing to the believers.”

And He said:

“Beautified for people is the love of desired things—women,”

through to His words:

“Say, ‘Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those mindful of Allah, there are gardens with their Lord beneath which rivers flow.’”

“Say, ‘Who has forbidden the adornment Allah has brought forth for His servants, and the good things He has provided?’ Say, ‘They are for those who believe during worldly life, exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection.’”

We therefore say:

Know that what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, describes concerning his love for various kinds of desirable things, and his dislike of others, is comparable to the actions he commands and forbids. Love and dislike are the foundation of commanding and forbidding. This likewise parallels the reward he promises for good deeds and the punishment he threatens for evil deeds. His commands and prohibitions, promises and threats, love and dislike, rewards and punishments—all these are among … (1).

We have discussed matters relating to this principle at length in several places, since it concerns both the foundations of religion and its subsidiary matters. One of its most important branches is “the question of designations and rulings” concerning sinful Muslims: can reward and punishment both apply to the same individual, as Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah maintain, or can they not, as the majority of the Khawārij and Muʿtazilah maintain? Can one and the same thing be loved in one respect and disliked in another, praised in one respect and condemned in another? Scholars, including jurists, speculative theologians and others, have disagreed over this. The conflict between the texts arises only from the opposition between attributes that call for praise and those that call for blame

The Khawārij included him among those addressed by the texts threatening punishment, and so held that he would remain in the Fire forever, yet did not judge him to be an unbeliever. If something were purely good, it would not cause division; if it were purely evil, its nature would not be obscure. Rather, it causes discord because both are combined within it.

The same applies to “the question of divine decree,” which is another branch of this principle. Actions that actually occur despite Allah’s prohibition combine two aspects: He wills them, since they are among the things that exist, yet He does not love them; rather, He detests and hates them. They therefore affirmed that created things exist without His will.

Thus, when Ghaylān al-Qadarī said to Rabīah ibn Abī Abd al-Rahmān, “Rabīah, I ask you by Allah: do you think Allah loves to be disobeyed?” Rabīah replied, “Do you then think Allah is disobeyed against His will?” It was as though he had stuffed a stone into his mouth. His point was: “You have declared Him free of any love of sins, but in doing so you have stripped Him of will and power, and made Him subject to force and compulsion.”

Those who opposed the Qadariyyah said, “Rather, everything He wills, He also loves and approves.” Their position entailed that disbelief, wickedness, and disobedience are loved and approved by Allah.

They were asked, “Can there be a demand, a will, and a call without will, love, or approval? This combines two contradictories.” They were confounded. Thus, the former stripped the Lord of His act of creation, His power, and His all-encompassing will; the latter stripped Him of His love, His approval, His prescriptive will, and what His commands and prohibitions entail in this regard.

Just as those discussed earlier did not acknowledge that one and the same person could be both rewarded and punished, but held that he must be either rewarded or punished, so these groups did not acknowledge that one and the same act could be willed in one respect but not another—willed without being loved. Rather, they held that it must be either both willed and loved, or neither willed nor loved.

Just as they differed concerning the Creator’s attributes, they differed concerning the attributes of created beings. The former affirmed only one capacity, existing before the act, while the latter affirmed for the creature only one capacity, existing alongside the act. The former denied the effective capacity by which an act occurs; the latter denied the capacity relevant to religious obligation, on the basis of which Allah commands and forbids His servant. This is one of the fundamental grounds of their disagreement over “the question of imposing obligations beyond one’s capacity.”

They divided into the Magian Qadariyyah, who affirm divine commands and prohibitions but deny divine determination and decree; the polytheistic Qadariyyah, who are worse than the former, affirm divine determination and decree but reject divine commands and prohibitions, or some of them; and the satanic Qadariyyah, who acknowledge the command but regard this as a contradiction contrary to truth and wisdom. You find one group affirming this but not that, and another doing the reverse—or affirming both, yet believing them contradictory. They thus become bewildered, turning away from affirming both together and contradicting themselves by siding now with one and now with the other. You find this in questions of theology and belief, and in questions of will and worship: for example, the question of listening to sounds, the question of speech, and questions concerning the attributes and the speech of Allah Most High, among others.

The foundation of all this is justice: treating like cases alike. Allah says:

“We have certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance, so that people may uphold justice.”

We have discussed this at length and explained in several places that justice encompasses all religion, truth, and goodness. True justice, however, may be impossible or difficult either to discern or to put into practice, because equivalence in every respect may be unattainable or unknown. In such cases, what is required is whatever most closely resembles justice and comes nearest to it. This is the best course. Hence He, Glorified is He, says:

“And give full measure and weight with justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity.”

He was asked:

Regarding someone who refrains from costly fabrics, such as silk, lavishly finished linen, and similar materials: is there a reward for abstaining from these or not? Give us a ruling; may you be rewarded.

He answered:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. As for what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, such as silk, one is rewarded for abstaining from it, just as one is punished for using it. It is authentically established that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter.”

He also said concerning silk and gold:

“These are forbidden to the males of my ummah and permissible for its females.”

As for permissible things, one is rewarded for forgoing what is superfluous—that is, what one does not need for the good of one’s religion—just as extravagance in permissible things is prohibited. Allah Most High says:

“And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor miserly, but follow a middle course between the two.”

Allah Most High says of the inhabitants of the Fire:

“Indeed, before this they lived in luxury.”

“And they persisted in the great sin.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely, lest you be left blameworthy and destitute.”

And Allah Most High says: “And give

the near relative his due, and the needy and the traveler, and do not squander wastefully.”

“Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and Satan is ever ungrateful to his Lord.”

Extravagance in permissible things means exceeding proper bounds and is a form of forbidden transgression. Forgoing what is superfluous in them is a permissible form of asceticism. As for abstaining from permissible things altogether—for example, someone who refrains from eating meat or bread, drinking water, or wearing linen and cotton, wears only wool, and refrains from marrying women, believing this to be recommended asceticism—such a person is ignorant and misguided, akin to Christian ascetics.

Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love transgressors.”

“And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good, and fear Allah, in whom you believe.”

This verse was revealed because a group of the Companions had resolved to give up eating good things, such as meat and the like, and to forgo marriage. In the two Sahīh collections, Anas reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“What is the matter with men, one of whom says, ‘As for me, I fast and never break my fast,’ while another says, ‘As for me, I pray at night and never sleep,’ and another says, ‘As for me, I do not eat meat’? Yet I fast and break my fast, pray at night and sleep, marry women, and eat meat. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.”

translated_text:
In Sahīh al-Bukhārī, it is reported:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man standing in the sun. He asked, ‘What is he doing?’ They replied, ‘This is Abū Isrā’īl. He has vowed to remain standing, not to seek shade or speak, and to fast.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Tell him to seek shade, speak, sit down, and complete his fast.’”

Allah Most High says:

“O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided for you, and be grateful to Allah, if it is Him that you worship.”

He thus commanded people to eat good things and give thanks to Him. What is good is what benefits a person, while He has forbidden foul things, which are those that harm him. He commanded gratitude to Him, which consists in obeying Him by doing what He has commanded and avoiding what He has forbidden.

In Sahīh Muslim, it is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah is indeed pleased with a servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, and takes a drink and praises Him for it.”

Allah Most High says:

“Eat of the good things and do righteous deeds.”

Whoever eats good things but neither gives thanks nor does righteous deeds is subject to punishment for the obligations he has neglected, and those good things are not lawful for him. Allah has made them lawful only for those who use them to help them obey Him, not for those who use them to help them disobey Him. As Allah Most High says:

“There is no blame on those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have consumed, provided they fear Allah, believe, and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves those who do good.”

And Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend, said:

“And provide its people with fruits—those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day.” He said, “As for whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little while, then compel him to undergo the punishment of the Fire. What a wretched destination!”

For this reason, it is not permissible to help someone commit sins by providing him with lawful things—for example, giving bread and meat to someone who drinks wine with them and uses them to help him commit acts of indecency.

Whoever declares unlawful the good things Allah has made lawful—food, clothing, marriage, and the like—and believes that abstaining from them altogether is better than using them, even for someone who uses them to help him obey Allah, is a transgressor liable to punishment. This is for declaring unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made lawful, for worshipping Allah Most High through monasticism, for turning away from the Sunnah of Allah’s Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and for neglecting obligations. Whatever is indispensable to fulfilling an obligation is itself obligatory.

Likewise, whoever goes to excess in certain acts of worship—such as fasting continuously or persistently spending the night in prayer—until this leaves him too weak to fulfil some obligations deserves punishment. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr:

“Your own self has a right over you, your family has a right over you, and your wife has a right over you. So give everyone their due.”

The foundation of religion, then, is to fulfil obligations and refrain from what is forbidden. A servant has never drawn near

Recommended voluntary acts that do not prevent the fulfilment of obligations are among the means by which Allah raises a person’s rank. Forgoing superfluous permissible things—those not needed to perform an obligatory or recommended act—while giving others preference in their enjoyment is something for which Allah rewards a person. Whoever forgoes them merely out of miserliness, rather than to draw near to Allah, is not praiseworthy. Whoever abstains from a category of things Allah has permitted, seeking to draw near to Him through that abstention, is mistaken and misguided. Whoever enjoys the food and clothing Allah has permitted, displaying Allah’s blessings and using them to help him obey Allah, is rewarded for doing so.

As for the words of Allah Most High:

“Then, on that Day, you will surely be questioned about the blessings you enjoyed.”

This means being questioned about gratitude for those blessings. The servant will be required to give due thanks to Allah for the blessings he enjoyed. Allah, glorified be He, does not punish anyone for what He has permitted; rather, He punishes for neglecting a command or committing a forbidden act. These comprehensive principles clarify the matters mentioned above and others besides.

As for silk, it is forbidden for men except in certain specified cases. Whoever wears what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden is sinful. As for linen, cotton, and similar fabrics, whoever forgoes them despite needing them is ignorant and misguided, while whoever is extravagant in their use is blameworthy. Whoever adorns himself by wearing them to display Allah’s blessings upon him is praiseworthy for doing so.

For the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“When Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effects of His blessings upon him.”

He also said:

“Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.”

Whoever forgoes fine clothing out of humility before Allah—not out of miserliness or as an absolute commitment to abstaining from it—will be rewarded by Allah for doing so and clothed in robes of honour. Conspicuous dress is disliked, whether unusually grand or unusually humble. The early generations disliked both forms of conspicuous dress: the grand and the humble. It is stated in the hadith:

“Whoever wears a garment of notoriety, Allah will clothe him in a garment of humiliation.”

The best course lies between extremes. The same outward act may earn a person reward when performed with a righteous intention, or punishment when performed with a corrupt intention. Whoever performs Hajj on foot because he is strong enough to walk, and gives others preference by spending the money on them instead, receives two rewards: one for walking and another for giving others preference.

Whoever performs Hajj on foot out of miserliness with his money, thereby harming himself, incurs two sins: the sin of miserliness and the sin of harming himself. Whoever performs Hajj riding because he is too weak to walk, seeking thereby to rest and gain strength for worship, receives two rewards. Whoever performs Hajj riding while wronging the camel-driver and the porter incurs two sins.

“Whoever drags his lower garment out of arrogance, Allah will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.”

And Allah, glorified and exalted be He, knows best.

 كَخِيَاطَتِهِ لِلنِّسَاءِ وَإِنْ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ يَمَسُّهُ عِنْدَ الْخِيَاطَةِ فَإِنَّ هَذَا لَيْسَ مِنْ الْمُحَرَّمِ وَمِثْلُ ذَلِكَ صِنَاعَةُ. الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ لِمَنْ يَسْتَعْمِلُهُ اسْتِعْمَالًا مُبَاحًا. وَيَجُوزُ اسْتِعْمَالُ خُيُوطِ الْحَرِيرِ فِي لِبَاسِ الرِّجَالِ كَذَلِكَ يُبَاحُ الْعَلَمُ وَالسِّجَافُ وَنَحْوُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا جَاءَتْ بِهِ السُّنَّةُ بِالرُّخْصَةِ فِيهِ وَهُوَ مَا كَانَ مَوْضِعُ إصْبَعَيْنِ أَوْ ثَلَاثَةٍ أَوْ أَرْبَعَةٍ وَقَدْ كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ جُبَّةٌ مَكْفُوفَةٌ بِحَرِيرِ.
translated_text:
He replied:

Praise be to Allah. It is not permissible to sew silk garments for someone who will wear them in a forbidden manner, such as a man wearing pure silk outside warfare and for no medicinal purpose, for this constitutes cooperation in sin and transgression. The same applies to making gold and silver vessels, according to the sounder of the two views held among the majority of scholars. It likewise applies to making instruments of amusement, images of living beings, idols, crosses, and similar things fashioned in a form in which their use is forbidden. The same applies to making wine. As for places of sin, unbelief, and the like, payment received for such unlawful work is illicit, and such conduct must be denounced.

However, sewing silk garments for someone who will wear them lawfully is permissible. This includes sewing them for women, even though the man touches the silk while sewing, since this is not forbidden. The same applies to crafting gold and silver items for someone who will use them lawfully.

It is permissible to use silk thread in men’s clothing. Decorative bands, edging, and similar features are likewise permissible within the allowance established by the Sunnah: an area two, three, or four fingers wide. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had a robe edged with silk.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:

فَأَجَابَ:
نَعَمْ إذَا أَعَانَ الرَّجُلُ عَلَى مَعْصِيَةِ اللَّهِ كَانَ آثِمًا؛ لِأَنَّهُ أَعَانَ عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ. وَلِهَذَا لَعَنَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الْخَمْرَ وَعَاصِرَهَا وَمُعْتَصِرَهَا وَحَامِلَهَا وَالْمَحْمُولَةَ إلَيْهِ وَبَائِعَهَا وَمُشْتَرِيَهَا وَسَاقِيَهَا وَشَارِبَهَا وَآكِلَ ثَمَنِهَا. وَأَكْثَرُ هَؤُلَاءِ كَالْعَاصِرِ وَالْحَامِلِ وَالسَّاقِي إنَّمَا هُمْ يُعَاوِنُونَ عَلَى شُرْبِهَا؛ وَلِهَذَا يُنْهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ السِّلَاحِ لِمَنْ يُقَاتِلُ بِهِ قِتَالًا مُحَرَّمًا كَقِتَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَالْقَتَّالِ فِي الْفِتْنَةِ فَإِذَا كَانَ هَذَا فِي الْإِعَانَةِ عَلَى الْمَعَاصِي فَكَيْفَ بِالْإِعَانَةِ عَلَى الْكُفْرِ وَشَعَائِرِ الْكُفْرِ. وَالصَّلِيبُ لَا يَجُوزُ عَمَلُهُ بِأُجْرَةِ وَلَا غَيْرِ أُجْرَةٍ وَلَا بَيْعُهُ صَلِيبًا كَمَا لَا يَجُوزُ بَيْعُ الْأَصْنَامِ وَلَا عَمَلُهَا.
 كَمَا ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 " {إنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَ بَيْعَ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْتَةَ وَالْخِنْزِيرَ
translated_text:
He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was also asked:

A tailor sewed a silk strap bearing a gold cross for Christians. Does he incur sin by sewing it? Is his payment lawful or not?

He replied:

Yes. If a man assists in disobedience to Allah, he incurs sin because he has cooperated in sin and transgression. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one for whom it is pressed, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, its seller, its buyer, the one who serves it, the one who drinks it, and the one who consumes its proceeds. Most of these people—such as the one who presses it, carries it, or serves it—merely assist in its consumption.

For this reason, selling weapons to someone who will use them in unlawful fighting, such as fighting Muslims or fighting during civil strife, is forbidden. If this applies to assisting in sins, then how much more so to assisting in unbelief and its religious observances!

It is not permissible to make a cross, whether for payment or without payment, nor to sell it as a cross, just as it is not permissible to sell or make idols.

As recorded in the authentic collection, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Indeed, Allah has forbidden the sale of wine, carrion, swine

وَسُئِلَ:
عَمَّنْ يَتَّجِرُ فِي الأقباع:
 هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ بَيْعُ الْقُبَعِ المرعزي وَشِرَاؤُهُ؟ وَالِاكْتِسَاءُ مِنْهُ؟ وَمَا يَجْرِي مَجْرَاهُ مِنْ الْحَرِيرِ الصَّامِتِ؟ أَوْ يُحَرَّمُ عَلَيْهِ لِكَوْنِ الْقُبَعِ لُبْسُ الرِّجَالِ دُونَ النِّسَاءِ؟ وَهَلْ يَجُوزُ بَيْعُهُ لِلْجُنْدِ وَالصِّبْيَانِ إذَا كَانُوا دُونَ الْبُلُوغِ؟ أَوْ لِلْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى أَمْ لَا؟ إلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْمَسَائِلِ.
فَأَجَابَ:
أَمَّا أقباع الْحَرِيرِ فَيَحْرُمُ لُبْسُهَا عَلَى الرِّجَالِ وَلِأَنَّهَا حَرِيرٌ
translated_text:
and idols.”

It is also established that he cursed image-makers, and that whenever he saw an image in the house, he cut it out. Thus, the maker of a cross is accursed: Allah and His Messenger have cursed him.

Anyone who receives payment for a forbidden object or a service already rendered—such as payment for carrying wine, making a cross, prostitution, or the like—must give it away in charity and repent of that forbidden work. Giving the payment away in charity will be an expiation for what he has done. He may not benefit from this payment, because it is an unlawful earning. Nor is it returned to the person who paid it, since that person has already received what he paid for. Rather, it is given away in charity. This has been expressly stated by a number of scholars: Imam Ahmad stated it concerning such cases as carrying wine, as did the scholars of Mālik’s school and others.

He was also asked about someone who trades in hoods:

Is it permissible for him to buy and sell fine goat-wool hoods, and to wear them, as well as similar articles made of sāmit silk? Or is this forbidden to him because hoods are men’s clothing, not women’s? Is it permissible to sell them to soldiers and to boys who have not reached puberty, or to Jews and Christians, or not? Other related questions were also raised.

He replied:

As for silk hoods, it is forbidden for men to wear them because they are silk.

original_text:
وَلُبْسُ الْحَرِيرِ حَرَامٌ عَلَى الرِّجَالِ بِسُنَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَإِجْمَاعِ الْعُلَمَاءِ. وَإِنْ كَانَ مُبَطَّنًا بِقُطْنِ أَوْ كَتَّانٍ. وَأَمَّا عَلَى النِّسَاءِ؛ فَلِأَنَّ الأقباع مِنْ لِبَاسِ الرِّجَالِ وَقَدْ لَعَنَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ الْمُتَشَبِّهَاتِ مِنْ النِّسَاءِ بِالرِّجَالِ والمتشبهين مِنْ الرِّجَالِ بِالنِّسَاءِ.

translated_text:
and wearing silk is forbidden to men by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the consensus of the scholars, even if it is lined with cotton or linen. As for women, these hoods are forbidden because they are men’s clothing, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, cursed women who imitate men and men who imitate women.

As for boys who have not reached puberty wearing silk, scholars hold two well-known views. The stronger view, however, is that it is not permissible. Whatever a man is forbidden to do himself, he is also forbidden to allow a young child to do. He must instruct the child to pray when he reaches seven and strike him for neglecting it when he reaches ten. How, then, could it be lawful for him to dress the child in forbidden garments?

When ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb saw a son of al-Zubayr wearing a silk garment, he tore it and said:

“Do not dress them in silk.”

Likewise, Ibn Masʿūd tore a silk garment that his son was wearing. Whatever is forbidden to wear is also unlawful to make or sell to someone who will wear it and to whom the prohibition applies. There is no distinction in this regard between soldiers and others. A man may not earn a living by sewing silk garments for someone who is forbidden to wear them, for that is assisting in sin and transgression, just like assisting in acts of indecency and the like. “ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb sent silk that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had given him to a polytheist.”

He was asked:

“Is it disliked to drape a coat over one’s shoulders without putting one’s arms through its sleeves?”

He replied:

“There is nothing wrong with this, by agreement of the jurists, who have explicitly stated that it is permissible. This is not the disliked form of draping garments, because this manner of dress is not that of the Jews.”

He was asked:

“Is it permissible for trousers to extend below the ankles?”

He replied:

“If a shirt, trousers, or any other garment is overlong, one may not let it extend below the ankles, as established hadiths from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, indicate. He said:

‘Letting garments hang below the ankles applies to trousers, waist wrappers, and shirts.’

That is, he forbade letting them hang below the ankles.”

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“What is the ruling on women wearing a kūfiyya cap with a dā’ir and a farq? And on their wearing farājī robes? What determines whether clothing constitutes imitation of men? Is the criterion what was worn during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or the customs of each respective age?”

He replied:

“Praise be to Allah. The kūfiyya cap with a farq and a dā’ir, worn without covering the loose-hanging hair, is boys’ attire, and a woman wearing it is imitating them. The first woman to adopt this style may have intended to imitate beardless youths, just as some prostitutes deliberately braid their hair into a single plait hanging between their shoulders, let locks hang down the sides of their faces, and wear turbans, so as to resemble beardless youths in their turbans, sideburns, and hair. A free woman may subsequently adopt some of these practices without that intention; nevertheless, she is thereby imitating men.

“Numerous reports from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, transmitted in the collections of authentic hadith and elsewhere, state that he cursed women who imitate men and men who imitate women. One narration states:

‘He cursed effeminate men and those who imitate men among

women.’ He also ordered the banishment of effeminate men. Al-Shāfiʿī, Ahmad, and others explicitly prescribed their banishment, saying: ‘The Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prescribes banishment as part of the prescribed punishment for unlawful sexual intercourse, and the banishment of effeminate men.’

In Sahīh Muslim, he is reported to have said:

‘There are two kinds of people of the Fire from my community whom I have not yet seen: women who are clothed yet naked, swaying and causing others to sway, with what look like the humps of Bactrian camels on their heads. They will neither enter Paradise nor smell its fragrance. And men carrying whips like cows’ tails, with which they beat Allah’s servants.’

The Sunan collections report that he

‘passed by Umm Salama’s door while she was wrapping her head, and said: “Umm Salama, one wrap, not two.”’

His words ‘clothed yet naked’ have been explained as referring to a woman who wears something that does not conceal her: she is clothed, yet in reality naked. Examples include a woman wearing a thin garment through which her skin shows, or a tight garment that reveals the contours of her body, such as her buttocks, forearm, and the like. A woman’s clothing is truly clothing only when it conceals her, revealing neither her body nor the shape of its parts, because it is thick and loose.

From this, the criterion governing his prohibition—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—of men imitating women and women imitating men becomes clear. If the distinction between men’s and women’s clothing rested solely on what women or men habitually wore according to their own choice and desire, women would not have been required to draw their outer cloaks over themselves or their head-coverings over their chests, nor would they have been forbidden to display themselves as in the former days of ignorance, since that had been those women’s custom.

Nor is the criterion a particular form of clothing specified in a statement of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or established by the customary dress of men and women in his time, such that one could say: “This alone is obligatory, and anything else is forbidden.” Women in his time wore garments with hems long enough to trail behind them when they went out, whereas men were commanded to raise their hems so that they did not reach the ankles.

Indeed, on this account, it is reported that he granted a concession whereby, if a woman dragged her hem over an unclean place and then passed with it over a clean place, it would thereby become purified. This is the position of a group of scholars within Ahmad’s school and elsewhere. The trailing hem is treated like a sandal, which frequently comes into contact with impurity and can therefore be purified with solid material, just as the two bodily outlets can be purified with solid material because of their repeated contact with impurity.

This, however, is not the only way to achieve covering. If a woman wore trousers or roomy, stiff leather boots, such as mūqs, with her outer cloak hanging over them so that the shape of her feet was not visible, this would fulfill the intended purpose. This differs from soft leather boots that reveal the shape of the foot, for these belong to men’s attire. Likewise, if a woman wore a long coat and a fur garment because she needed them to ward off the cold, she would not be forbidden to do so.

If someone were to say, “Women did not use to wear fur garments,” we would reply: “That depends on need. In cold countries, clothing needs to be thick and warm, even though this is not needed in hot countries.”

He thus made imitation the basis of the ruling: each sex adopting the characteristics of the other.

We have discussed this principle at length in The Requirement of the Straight Path to Differ from the People of Hellfire, explaining that resemblance in outward matters gives rise to affinity and similarity in character and conduct. For this reason, we have been forbidden to imitate disbelievers, non-Arabs, and Bedouins, and men and women have each been forbidden to imitate the other sex, as in the hadith traced back to the Prophet:

“Whoever imitates a people is one of them.”

“Whoever imitates those other than us is not one of us.”

A man who imitates women acquires their characteristics in proportion to his imitation, until this leads him to complete effeminacy and to allowing himself to be used as though he were a woman. Since singing was a precursor to this and was something women did, they used to call male singers effeminate men.

A woman who imitates men acquires their characteristics, until she comes to display herself, appear publicly, and join men in their activities to such an extent that some women may expose their bodies as men do, seek to place themselves above men as men place themselves above women, and engage in conduct incompatible with the modesty and reserve prescribed for women. This much may result from mere resemblance.

He was asked:

Are these turbans that women wear on their heads forbidden or disliked? What turbans are recommended for women? And may they wear leather socks?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah alone.

These turbans worn by women are undoubtedly forbidden. It is authentically reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Two groups from my community will be among the people of the Fire, whom I have not yet seen: women who are clothed yet naked, going astray and leading others astray, with something on their heads resembling the humps of Khurasanian camels. They will neither enter Paradise nor smell its fragrance. And men carrying whips like cattle’s tails, with which they beat Allah’s servants.”

He was asked:

What if someone prays in a ritually impure place?

He answered:

If someone prays with part of his body in a ritually impure place, being unable to pray anywhere else, he is excused and his prayer is valid. But if he can pray in a ritually pure place, he is not permitted to pray in the impure place.

{أَنَّهُ نَهَى عَنْ الصَّلَاةِ فِي سَبْعِ مَوَاطِنَ: الْمَقْبَرَةِ وَالْمَجْزَرَةِ وَالْمَزْبَلَةِ وَقَارِعَةِ الطَّرِيقِ وَالْحَمَّامِ وَظَهْرِ الْبَيْتِ الْحَرَامِ}
 وَهَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعُ - غَيْرُ ظَهْرِ بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ - قَدْ يُعَلِّلُهَا بَعْضُ الْفُقَهَاءِ بِأَنَّهَا مَظِنَّةُ النَّجَاسَةِ. وَبَعْضُهُمْ يَجْعَلُ النَّهْيَ تَعَبُّدًا.
translated_text:
He was asked:

Are there any places on earth where prayer is disliked?

He answered:

Yes. Prayer is prohibited in certain places. It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked about praying in camel enclosures. He said:

“Do not pray in them.”

He was asked about praying in sheep pens and said:

“Pray in them.”

It is reported in the Sunan that he said:

“The whole earth is a place of prayer, except graveyards and bathhouses.”

It is also reported in the Sahīh that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“May Allah curse the Jews and Christians: they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship.”

He was warning against what they had done.

It is also reported in the Sahīh that he said:

“Those who came before you used to take graves as places of worship. Beware! Do not take graves as places of worship, for I forbid you to do so.”

It is reported in the Sunan that he forbade prayer on land that had been swallowed up by the earth.

In Sunan Ibn Mājah and elsewhere, it is reported that he forbade prayer in seven places: graveyards, slaughterhouses, refuse dumps, public thoroughfares, bathhouses, and the roof of the Sacred House.

Some jurists explain the prohibition concerning these places—apart from the roof of Allah’s Sacred House—on the grounds that they are likely to contain ritual impurities. Others regard the prohibition as a purely devotional injunction.

original_text:
وَالصَّحِيحُ أَنَّ عِلَلَهَا مُخْتَلِفَةٌ. تَارَةً تَكُونُ الْعِلَّةُ مُشَابَهَةَ أَهْلِ الشِّرْكِ.
 كَالصَّلَاةِ عِنْدَ الْقُبُورِ وَتَارَةً لِكَوْنِهَا مَأْوًى لِلشَّيَاطِينِ:
 كَأَعْطَانِ الْإِبِلِ. وَتَارَةً لِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ الْحَمَّامِ إذَا اُضْطُرَّ الْمُسْلِمُ لِلصَّلَاةِ فِيهَا وَخَافَ فَوَاتَ الْوَقْتِ هَلْ يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ أَنْ يَغْتَسِلَ وَيَخْرُجَ وَيُصَلِّيَ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ الْوَقْتُ فَإِنَّهُ يَغْتَسِلُ وَيُصَلِّي بِالْحَمَّامِ؛ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ فِي الْأَمَاكِنِ الْمَنْهِيِّ عَنْهَا فِي الْوَقْتِ أَوْلَى مِنْ الصَّلَاةِ بَعْدَ الْوَقْتِ فِي غَيْرِهَا وَلِهَذَا لَوْ حُبِسَ فِي الْحُشِّ صَلَّى فِيهِ وَفِي الْإِعَادَةِ نِزَاعٌ. وَالصَّحِيحُ أَنَّهُ لَا إعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ؛ وَلِهَذَا يُصَلِّي فِي الْوَقْتِ عُرْيَانَا إذَا لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ إلَّا كَذَلِكَ. وَأَمَّا إنْ أَمْكَنَهُ الِاغْتِسَالُ وَالْخُرُوجُ لِلصَّلَاةِ خَارِجَ الْحَمَّامِ فِي الْوَقْتِ لَمْ يَجُزْ لَهُ الصَّلَاةُ فِي الْحَمَّامِ وَكَذَلِكَ لَوْ أَمْكَنَهُ الِاغْتِسَالُ فِي بَيْتِهِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُصَلِّي فِي الْحَمَّامِ إلَّا لِحَاجَةِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
The correct view, however, is that the reasons for these prohibitions differ. Sometimes the reason is resemblance to the polytheists, as with prayer at graves; sometimes it is that these places are refuges for devils, as with camel enclosures; and sometimes it is something else. Allah knows best.

He was asked:

If a Muslim has no choice but to pray in a bathhouse and fears that the prayer time will expire, is it permissible for him to do so?

He answered:

If he cannot bathe, leave, and pray before the prayer time expires, he should bathe and pray in the bathhouse. Praying within the prescribed time in places where prayer is prohibited is preferable to praying elsewhere after the time has expired. Thus, if someone is confined in a latrine, he should pray there. There is disagreement over whether he must repeat the prayer, but the correct view is that he need not repeat it. Likewise, a person should pray unclothed within the prescribed time if he cannot do otherwise.

However, if he can bathe, leave the bathhouse, and pray outside it within the prescribed time, he may not pray in the bathhouse. Similarly, if he can bathe at home, he may not pray in the bathhouse except when there is a need. Allah knows best.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ الصَّلَاةِ فِي الْحَمَّامِ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
فِي سُنَنِ أَبِي دَاوُد وَغَيْرِهِ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 " 
{الْأَرْضُ كُلُّهَا مَسْجِدٌ إلَّا الْمَقْبَرَةَ وَالْحَمَّامَ}
 وَقَدْ صَحَّحَهُ الْحُفَّاظُ. وَأَمَّا إنْ ضَاقَ الْوَقْتُ فَهَلْ يُصَلِّي فِي الْحَمَّامِ؟ أَوْ يُفَوِّتُ الصَّلَاةَ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ فَيُصَلِّيَ خَارِجَهَا؟ عَلَى قَوْلَيْنِ فِي مَذْهَبِ أَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِ. فَلَا يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ. وَيَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ إنْ احْتَاجَ إلَى الْحَمَّامِ أَنْ يَغْتَسِلَ فِي أَوَّلِ الْوَقْتِ وَيَخْرُجَ يُصَلِّي ثُمَّ إنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُتِمَّ اغْتِسَالَهُ بِالسِّدْرِ وَنَحْوِهِ عَادَ إلَى الْحَمَّامِ وَجُمْهُورُ الْعُلَمَاءِ عَلَى أَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ فِيهَا مَنْهِيٌّ عَنْهَا؛
 إمَّا نَهْيَ تَحْرِيمٍ أَوْ لَا تَصِحُّ:
 كَالْمَشْهُورِ مِنْ مَذْهَبِ أَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِ. وَإِمَّا نَهْيَ تَنْزِيهٍ كَمَذْهَبِ الشَّافِعِيِّ وَغَيْرِهِ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about praying in a bathhouse.

He answered:

In Sunan Abī Dāwūd and elsewhere, Abū Sa‘īd narrated that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The entire earth is a place of prayer except graveyards and bathhouses.”

The leading hadith scholars have graded this report authentic. If, however, little time remains, should one pray in the bathhouse, or let the prayer time expire until one leaves and prays outside? There are two opinions on this within the school of Ahmad and among others. Thus, one should not pray in a bathhouse.

Anyone in a state of major ritual impurity who needs to use a bathhouse should perform the ritual bath at the beginning of the prayer time, then leave and pray. If he then wishes to complete his washing with lote-tree leaves or the like, he may return to the bathhouse.

The majority of scholars hold that prayer there is prohibited: either it is forbidden or invalid, as in the well-known position of Ahmad’s school and others, or it is merely disliked, as in the school of al-Shāfi‘ī and others.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ:
هَلْ لَهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ، إذَا خَافَ خُرُوجَ الْوَقْتِ؟ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
أَمَّا إذَا ذَهَبَ إلَى الْحَمَّامِ لِيَغْتَسِلَ وَيَخْرُجَ وَيُصَلِّيَ خَارِجَ الْحَمَّامِ فِي الْوَقْتِ فَلَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ إلَّا أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ أَوْ تَفُوتَ الصَّلَاةُ فَالصَّلَاةُ فِي الْحَمَّامِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ تَفْوِيتِ الصَّلَاةِ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ فِي الْحَمَّامِ كَالصَّلَاةِ فِي الْحُشِّ وَالْمَوَاضِعِ النَّجِسَةِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ. وَمَنْ كَانَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ نَجِسٍ وَلَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنْهُ حَتَّى يَفُوتَ الْوَقْتُ فَإِنَّهُ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ وَلَا يُفَوِّتُ الْوَقْتَ لِأَنَّ مُرَاعَاةَ الْوَقْتِ مُقَدَّمَةٌ عَلَى مُرَاعَاةِ جَمِيعِ الْوَاجِبَاتِ. وَأَمَّا إنْ كَانَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ إذَا ذَهَبَ إلَى الْحَمَّامِ لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ الْخُرُوجُ حَتَّى يَخْرُجَ الْوَقْتُ فَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَتْ هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةُ وَالْأَظْهَرُ أَنَّهُ يُصَلِّي بِالتَّيَمُّمِ فَإِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ بِالتَّيَمُّمِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ الصَّلَاةِ فِي الْأَمَاكِنِ الَّتِي نُهِيَ عَنْهَا وَعَنْ الصَّلَاةِ بَعْدَ خُرُوجِ الْوَقْتِ.
translated_text:
He was also asked:

May a person pray in a bathhouse if he fears that the prayer time will expire, or not?

He answered:

If he goes to the bathhouse intending to bathe, leave, and pray outside within the prescribed time, but then finds himself with no choice but to pray in the bathhouse or miss the prayer, praying in the bathhouse is better than missing the prayer. Praying in a bathhouse is comparable to praying in a latrine, in places affected by ritual impurity, and the like. Whoever is in such an impure place and cannot leave it before the prayer time expires should pray there rather than let the time expire, because observing the prescribed time takes precedence over observing all other obligations.

However, if he knows that, by going to the bathhouse, he will be unable to leave before the prayer time expires, this question has already been discussed. The stronger view is that he should perform tayammum (dry purification) and pray, for praying with tayammum is better than praying in places where prayer is prohibited or praying after the prescribed time has expired.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
هَلْ الصَّلَاةُ فِي الْبِيَعِ وَالْكَنَائِسِ جَائِزَةٌ مَعَ وُجُودِ الصُّوَرِ أَمْ لَا؟ وَهَلْ يُقَالُ إنَّهَا بُيُوتُ اللَّهِ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
لَيْسَتْ بُيُوتَ اللَّهِ وَإِنَّمَا بُيُوتُ اللَّهِ الْمَسَاجِدُ:
 بَلْ هِيَ بُيُوتٌ يُكْفَرُ فِيهَا بِاَللَّهِ وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا فَالْبُيُوتُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ أَهْلِهَا وَأَهْلُهَا كُفَّارٌ فَهِيَ بُيُوتُ عِبَادَةِ الْكُفَّارِ.
 وَأَمَّا الصَّلَاةُ فِيهَا فَفِيهَا ثَلَاثَةُ أَقْوَالٍ لِلْعُلَمَاءِ فِي مَذْهَبِ أَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِ:
 الْمَنْعُ مُطْلَقًا وَهُوَ قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ. وَالْإِذْنُ مُطْلَقًا وَهُوَ قَوْلُ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِ أَحْمَد.
 وَالثَّالِثُ:
 وَهُوَ الصَّحِيحُ الْمَأْثُورُ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ وَغَيْرِهِ وَهُوَ مَنْصُوصٌ عَنْ أَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِ أَنَّهُ إنْ كَانَ فِيهَا صُوَرٌ لَمْ يُصَلَّ فِيهَا لِأَنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ لَا تَدْخُلُ بَيْتًا فِيهِ صُورَةٌ وَلِأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمْ يَدْخُلْ الْكَعْبَةَ حَتَّى مُحِيَ مَا فِيهَا مِنْ الصُّوَرِ وَكَذَلِكَ قَالَ عُمَرُ: إنَّا كُنَّا لَا نَدْخُلُ كَنَائِسَهُمْ وَالصُّوَرُ فِيهَا. وَهِيَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْمَبْنِيِّ عَلَى الْقَبْرِ فَفِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ أَنَّهُ ذُكِرَ
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

Is it permissible to pray in churches and synagogues when images are present, or not? May they be called houses of Allah, or not?

He answered:

They are not houses of Allah; rather, the houses of Allah are the mosques. They are instead houses in which Allah is disbelieved in, even though He may also be remembered there. Buildings have the same status as their occupants, and their occupants are disbelievers; thus, they are the disbelievers’ houses of worship.

As for praying in them, scholars within Ahmad’s school and other schools hold three views:

The first is unconditional prohibition, which is Mālik’s view. The second is unconditional permission, which is the view of some scholars of Ahmad’s school.

The third—which is the correct view, transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb and others, and expressly stated by Ahmad and others—is that if images are present, one should not pray there. This is because the angels do not enter a house containing an image, and because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not enter the Kaaba until the images inside it had been effaced. Likewise, ʿUmar said: “We used not to enter their churches while images were in them.”

Such a place is comparable to a mosque built over a grave, for the two Sahīh collections report that mention was made

original_text:
لِلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ كَنِيسَةٌ بِأَرْضِ الْحَبَشَةِ وَمَا فِيهَا مِنْ الْحُسْنِ وَالتَّصَاوِيرِ فَقَالَ:
 " 
{أُولَئِكَ إذَا مَاتَ فِيهِمْ الرَّجُلُ الصَّالِحُ بَنَوْا عَلَى قَبْرِهِ مَسْجِدًا وَصَوَّرُوا فِيهِ تِلْكَ التَّصَاوِيرَ أُولَئِكَ شِرَارُ الْخَلْقِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ}
 وَأَمَّا إذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهَا صُوَرٌ فَقَدْ صَلَّى الصَّحَابَةُ فِي الْكَنِيسَةِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَمَّنْ يَبْسُطُ سَجَّادَةً فِي الْجَامِعِ وَيُصَلِّي عَلَيْهَا:
 هَلْ مَا فَعَلَهُ بِدْعَةٌ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، أَمَّا الصَّلَاةُ عَلَى السَّجَّادَةِ بِحَيْثُ يَتَحَرَّى الْمُصَلِّي ذَلِكَ فَلَمْ تَكُنْ هَذِهِ سُنَّةَ السَّلَفِ مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ وَمَنْ بَعْدَهُمْ مِنْ التَّابِعِينَ لَهُمْ بِإِحْسَانِ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَلْ كَانُوا يُصَلُّونَ فِي مَسْجِدِهِ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ لَا يَتَّخِذُ أَحَدُهُمْ سَجَّادَةً يَخْتَصُّ بِالصَّلَاةِ عَلَيْهَا.
 وَقَدْ رُوِيَ أَنَّ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ مَهْدِيٍّ لَمَّا قَدِمَ الْمَدِينَةَ بَسَطَ سَجَّادَةً فَأَمَرَ مَالِكٌ بِحَبْسِهِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ:
 إنَّهُ عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ مَهْدِيٍّ فَقَالَ: أَمَا عَلِمْت أَنَّ بَسْطَ السَّجَّادَةِ فِي مَسْجِدِنَا بِدْعَةٌ. وَفِي الصَّحِيحِ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الخدري فِي حَدِيثِ اعْتِكَافِ النَّبِيِّ
translated_text:
to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, of a church in Abyssinia, its beauty, and the images within it. He said:

“When a righteous man among those people died, they would build a place of worship over his grave and make those images inside it. Those are the worst of creation before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

If, however, there are no images in a church, the Companions did pray in churches. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Regarding someone who spreads out a prayer mat in the congregational mosque and prays on it: is what he has done an innovation or not?

He answered:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all worlds. As for deliberately choosing to pray on a prayer mat, this was not the practice of the early generations—the Emigrants, the Helpers, and those who followed them in righteousness. During the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, they would instead pray directly on the ground in his mosque. None of them had a personal mat reserved for praying on.

It is related that when ʿAbd al-Rahmān ibn Mahdī came to Medina, he spread out a prayer mat, so Mālik ordered that he be detained. Mālik was told, “He is ʿAbd al-Rahmān ibn Mahdī.” He said, “Did you not know that spreading out a prayer mat in our mosque is an innovation?”

In the Sahīh, it is narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, in the account of the Prophet’s devotional retreat

This hadith makes clear that a person would protect himself from the intense heat simply by spreading out part of a garment he was wearing—such as his waist-wrapper, upper wrap, or shirt—and prostrating on it. This makes clear that they did not pray on prayer rugs, or even on any intervening covering. Thus, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions would sometimes pray in their sandals

and sometimes barefoot, as reported in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and the Musnad from Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“He prayed and took off his sandals, so the people took off theirs. This shows that they prayed in their sandals and that they did so in the mosque, since they were not walking in them over floor coverings. It also shows that if someone sees filth on his sandals, he should wipe them on the ground and pray in them. He need not wash them, nor take them off at prayer time and place his feet on them, as many people do.

The Sunnah supports all of this. In the two Sahīh collections and the Musnad, Abū Salama Sa'īd ibn Yazīd said:

“I asked Anas, ‘Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray in his sandals?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’”

In Sunan Abī Dāwūd, Shaddād ibn Aws reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Differ from the Jews, for they do not pray in their sandals or leather socks.”

He thus commanded us to act differently from them in this respect, since they remove their leather socks and sandals when praying. According to what is reported about them, they follow the example of Moses, peace be upon him, who was told when Allah spoke privately to him:

“Take off your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwā.”

Thus, we were forbidden to imitate them

and were commanded to pray in our leather socks and sandals and, if there was any filth on them, to wipe them on the ground, as indicated by the evidence already mentioned.

Further evidence is what Abū Dāwūd also narrated from Abū Hurayra: the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“If any of you steps on filth in his sandals, the earth purifies them.”

Another wording states:

“If he steps on filth in his leather socks, the earth purifies them.”

A report conveying the same meaning was also narrated from ‘Ā’isha, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The hadith of ‘Ā’isha has been graded good.

As for the hadith of Abū Hurayra, its second wording was transmitted through Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlān. Al-Bukhārī included his narrations as corroborating reports, and Muslim included them as supporting transmissions. More than one scholar declared him trustworthy. The narrator of the first wording was not named; nevertheless, its multiple routes of transmission, with neither grounds for suspicion nor contradiction of more reliable reports, mean that it too is good.

This is the sounder of the scholars’ two views. Besides being supported by the Sunnah, it is also what sound reasoning requires: since this is a surface that repeatedly comes into contact with impurity, removing the impurity from it with a solid substance suffices. It is comparable to the two bodily outlets, which may be adequately cleansed with stones, as established by mass-transmitted reports in the Sunnah, even when water is available. The Muslims have unanimously agreed that cleansing oneself with stones is permissible.

This is further demonstrated by the fact that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his Companions used to pray
