Umar’s sobbing could be heard from behind the rows when he recited:

“I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.”

Sobbing means weeping aloud, as explained by Abū Ubayd. This report from Umar is well established and was mentioned by Mālik, Ahmad and others. This disagreement concerns cases in which the person is not overcome involuntarily.

As for sneezing, weeping or yawning that a worshipper cannot control, the correct view according to the majority is that it does not invalidate prayer. This is the explicit position of Ahmad and others. Some of his followers, however, held that it invalidates prayer even though the person is excused, as with someone who speaks out of forgetfulness. Regarding speech uttered out of forgetfulness, two opinions are reported from Ahmad. The first, which is also Abū Hanīfa’s position, is that it invalidates prayer.

And the second, which is the position of Mālik and al-Shāfi‘ī, is that it does not invalidate prayer. This is the stronger view. Involuntary sneezing and similar occurrences warrant this ruling even more than forgetful speech, since they are ordinary occurrences that a person cannot prevent. It is authentically established that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Yawning is from Satan. When one of you yawns, let him suppress it as much as he can.”

There is also the established report of the man who sneezed during prayer and for whom Mu‘āwiya ibn al-Hakam al-Sulamī invoked Allah’s mercy. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade Mu‘āwiya to speak during prayer, but said nothing to the man who sneezed. To hold that sneezing invalidates prayer is to impose a burden; it is one of the newly introduced views with no basis in what is transmitted from the early generations, may Allah be pleased with them.

It has thus become clear that these throat sounds, which convey no conventionally assigned meaning, are disputed within the schools of Abū Hanīfa, Mālik and Ahmad. The stronger view concerning all of them is that they do not invalidate prayer. Sounds are comparable to movements: just as minor movement does not invalidate prayer, neither does a slight sound. Loud laughter, however, is different, for it is comparable to minor movement, and that is incompatible with prayer. Indeed, loud laughter is even more incompatible with the purpose of prayer. Hence it is never permissible during prayer, unlike extensive movement, which is permitted in cases of necessity. And Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ:
عَمَّا إذَا قَرَأَ الْقُرْآنَ وَيَعُدُّ فِي الصَّلَاةِ بِسُبْحَةِ هَلْ تَبْطُلُ صَلَاتُهُ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
إنْ كَانَ الْمُرَادُ بِهَذَا السُّؤَالِ أَنْ يَعُدَّ الْآيَاتِ أَوْ يَعُدَّ تَكْرَارَ السُّورَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِ:
 
{قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ}
 بِالسُّبْحَةِ فَهَذَا لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ وَإِنْ أُرِيدَ بِالسُّؤَالِ شَيْءٌ آخَرُ فَلْيُبَيِّنْهُ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
هَلْ لِلْإِنْسَانِ إذَا دَخَلَ الْمَسْجِدَ وَالنَّاسُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ أَنْ يَجْهَرَ بِالسَّلَامِ أَوْ لَا؟ خَشْيَةَ أَنْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِ مَنْ هُوَ جَاهِلٌ بِالسَّلَامِ.
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، إنْ كَانَ الْمُصَلِّي يُحْسِنُ الرَّدَّ بِالْإِشَارَةِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ فَلَا بَأْسَ كَمَا كَانَ الصَّحَابَةُ يُسَلِّمُونَ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَهُوَ يَرُدُّ عَلَيْهِمْ بِالْإِشَارَةِ وَإِنْ لَمْ يُحْسِنْ الرَّدَّ بَلْ قَدْ يَتَكَلَّمُ فَلَا يَنْبَغِي إدْخَالُهُ فِيمَا يَقْطَعُ صَلَاتَهُ أَوْ يَتْرُكُ بِهِ الرَّدَّ الْوَاجِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

If someone recites the Quran during prayer and keeps count using prayer beads, does this invalidate his prayer?

He replied:

If the question means using prayer beads to count verses or repetitions of a single surah, such as “Say: He is Allah, the One,” there is nothing wrong with that. If something else is intended by the question, let the questioner clarify it. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

When someone enters the mosque while people are praying, may he greet them aloud, or should he refrain for fear that someone unaware of the ruling might return his greeting verbally?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If the person praying knows how to respond with a gesture, there is nothing wrong with greeting him, just as the Companions used to greet the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he would respond to them with a gesture. But if he does not know how to respond and might speak instead, one should not put him in a situation where he either invalidates his prayer or fails to give the response required of him. And Allah knows best.

عَنْ الْمُرُورِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ الْمَأْمُومِ:
 هَلْ هُوَ فِي النَّهْيِ كَغَيْرِهِ مِثْلَ الْإِمَامِ وَالْمُنْفَرِدِ أَمْ لَا؟

translated_text:
He was asked:

Does the prohibition against passing in front of someone praying apply to a person praying behind an imam, just as it applies to the imam and someone praying alone?

He replied:

The prohibition applies only to passing in front of the imam or someone praying alone. They cited as evidence the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās—may Allah be pleased with them both. And Allah knows best.
